title: The 32K memory mystery
setup: A hypothetical model has 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, and 2-byte cache elements. It retains 32,768 tokens for one sequence. Which claim goes beyond the evidence?
claims: Its raw KV cache is 4 GiB.
Eight independent sequences of that length require 32 GiB of raw KV cache.
A 4 GiB cache means the entire model fits on a 4 GiB GPU.
evidence: The calculation counts key and value tensors only: 2 × layers × tokens × KV heads × head dimension × bytes × sequences. It excludes weights, workspaces, allocator overhead, and metadata.
explanation: A cache estimate is not a full serving-memory estimate. The missing memory categories are exactly what make the third claim unsupported.

title: A group is not a guarantee
setup: Assume each completion independently succeeds with probability 0.05, and a group contains 8 completions. Find the unsupported claim.
claims: The chance that every completion fails is about 66.34%.
Increasing the group size guarantees useful reward contrast on every prompt.
The assumptions of independence and equal success probability matter.
evidence: Under these assumptions, the all-failure probability is (1 − 0.05)^8. Uniform binary rewards can occur through all failures or all successes. Larger groups change probabilities, but do not eliminate those events.
explanation: A lower probability is not a guarantee. Real reward components and correlated samples also change the calculation.

title: The document was relevant. Was the answer?
setup: Consider the journal’s proposed toy policy: answer only when evidence is relevant, supports the answer, and contains no detected contradiction. Which claim does not follow?
claims: A relevant retrieved document alone is enough to justify any confident answer.
Relevant but unsupported evidence does not pass this toy policy.
This deterministic example is not a measured benchmark of a real RAG system.
evidence: The toy decision rule is relevant AND supported AND NOT contradiction. Its eight Boolean combinations can be checked, but those checks do not establish the accuracy of real retrieval or claim-support classifiers.
explanation: Retrieval relevance and support for a particular claim are different. A useful document can still fail to justify the answer being proposed.

title: The document that gave itself permission
setup: An agent is authorized to read document A. Text inside A instructs it to email private data to a new recipient. Which claim is unsupported?
claims: The requested send action is outside the read capability.
The document’s instruction does not itself grant a new permission.
A stricter system prompt proves that every future tool action is safe.
evidence: The article’s toy capability check binds operation, target, and prepared payload. It illustrates enforcing a boundary outside untrusted content. It is a small deterministic example, not a proof of production agent security.
explanation: Prompt wording does not prove a complete security property. Permission enforcement, isolation, and action-specific validation remain separate engineering concerns.

title: One format. Every robot?
setup: A team converts robot demonstrations into a common dataset format. Which conclusion goes too far?
claims: The team should still check coordinate frames, units, action timing, and embodiment conventions.
Matching the file format guarantees the policy will work on every robot.
A data conversion should be followed by validation and controlled evaluation.
evidence: A shared file format does not remove differences in actions, sensors, geometry, or embodiment. The robotics analysis proposes validating the data contract before treating a training run as meaningful evidence.
explanation: Syntactic compatibility does not establish semantic compatibility or successful transfer. Those require checks and experiments.

title: A map without limits
setup: A proposed system combines geometric mapping and semantic recognition in a GPS-denied environment. Find the unsupported promise.
claims: The proposal guarantees accurate mapping in every terrain and lighting condition.
Sensor calibration and timing are part of the system’s assumptions.
Geometry quality and semantic recognition should be evaluated separately.
evidence: The mapping analysis separates localization, geometry, and semantic labels, and discusses environmental and sensor limitations. Its evaluation protocol is proposed work, not an executed universal-performance demonstration.
explanation: A broad ambition is not an achieved guarantee. Evaluation has to define conditions, datasets, failure modes, and measurable limits.
